input.description: Show POST owners pipeline and throwers

content.content:
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# An 'Idempotency-Key' already seen returns the original owner (200) via 'existing';
# otherwise 'proceed' runs the normal create pipeline. First so a repeat short-circuits
# before body validation and before the duplicate-identity check (which would be 409).
idempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerIdempotency
  govern: [ transaction ]
  outputs:
    existing: respondExisting
    proceed: normalizeAddress

respondExisting:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]

normalizeAddress:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerAddress
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: validate

validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateRequiredOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: validatePostcode

validatePostcode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerPostcode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectFutureRegistrationDate

rejectFutureRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectFutureRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: resolveRegistrationDate

resolveRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ResolveOwnerRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectDailyLimit

rejectDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectDailyOwnerLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: rejectFullCity

rejectFullCity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RejectFullOwnerCity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: normalizeTelephone

normalizeTelephone:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
  govern: [ transaction ]

No other code paths emit those statuses — every 400/409/429 flows through an escalation handler. The change is complete.

## Summary

The specification requires that all rejection responses (400, 409, 429) return an RFC7807 `application/problem+json` body with `type`, `title`, `status`, and `detail`.

On inspection, nearly every rejection handler already produced a `ProblemDetail` via the shared `ProblemDetails.build(...)` helper. The **one exception** was `MissingOwnerFieldsExceptionHandler` (the 400 for missing/blank required owner fields — the exact path the new test exercises by removing `city`), which still returned a bespoke `MissingFieldsError` JSON record instead of problem+json.

**Change made** — `MissingOwnerFieldsExceptionHandler.java`:
- Now builds its body with the same `ProblemDetails.build(ex, HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, ...)` helper the other handlers use, so it gets the RFC7807 `type`/`title`/`status`/`detail` members and `application/problem+json` content type for free.
- Preserves the offending field names by attaching them as an `errors` property on the `ProblemDetail`, so no diagnostic information is lost.
- Removed the now-unused `MissingFieldsError` record.

This keeps the logic where it belongs (the shared `ProblemDetails` builder stays the single source of the common problem+json shape; the handler only adds its endpoint-specific `errors` detail) rather than duplicating the RFC7807 assembly.

Test suite: `BUILD SUCCESS`, `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — the new `coreRejectionIsProblemJson` acceptance test passes, asserting the 400 response is `application/problem+json` with `$.status == 400`.
